title: He Returned The Same Machine Five Times
script: A guy came into my store returning a five-hundred-dollar espresso machine, insisting it 'just stopped working' after three weeks, demanding a brand new replacement instead of the free repair our policy actually offers. I processed it because that's the job, but our warranty system logs a serial number on every claim, and something about his story felt rehearsed. I searched it. It was the same serial number, four returns, four different store locations, four different months, always the same claim, always a brand new box walking back out the door with him. He wasn't buying new machines and returning broken ones — he'd found one machine that never left his house, and just kept 'returning' it for a fresh one every time the warranty reset. I flagged the account company-wide with the pattern attached. He came back a fifth time, receipt in hand, and the register simply refused the return — right in front of the whole line, with his own serial number printed on the screen.

shots.news_angle: The espresso machine is being returned repeatedly by the customer as a faulty item.
